# A slice may be read at an offset from the loop index (a[i+1], a[i-1], a[i+off])
# as long as the loop does not also write it, so no iteration reads what another
# writes and the order does not matter. The length check is against the last index
# read, a short source still panics, and a copy from an offset is the copy builtin.
# Slices that share memory take the original loop. After a panic the slices are
# not compared: the rewritten loops check the lengths first and write nothing.

# The scalar program is the reference behavior.
exec go run ./testmain
cmp stdout testmain/output

cp ops.go ops.go.orig
loopvec -split .
! stdout .
cmpenv stderr stderr.want
cmp ops_simd.go ops_simd.go.want
cmp ops.go ops.go.guarded

# The simd build must behave identically.
env GOEXPERIMENT=simd
exec go run ./testmain
cmp stdout testmain/output

-- go.mod --
module example.com/test

go 1.27.1
-- ops.go --
package test

// Reads one element ahead of the store: nothing the loop writes is read.
func Diff(dst, a []float64) {
	for i := 0; i < len(dst)-1; i++ {
		dst[i] = a[i+1] - a[i]
	}
}

// Reads on both sides, and the same slice at three offsets.
func Smooth(dst, a []int32) {
	for i := 1; i < len(dst)-1; i++ {
		dst[i] = a[i-1] + a[i] + a[i+1]
	}
}

// The offset is a variable.
func Shift(dst, a []int32, off int) {
	for i := 0; i < len(dst); i++ {
		dst[i] = a[i+off] * 2
	}
}

// A copy from an offset.
func CopyShift(dst, src []int32) {
	for i := 0; i < len(dst); i++ {
		dst[i] = src[i+1]
	}
}

func CopyBehind(dst, src []int32) {
	for i := 2; i < len(dst); i++ {
		dst[i] = src[i-2]
	}
}

// A reduction over neighboring elements.
func SumPairs(a []int32) int32 {
	var s int32
	for i := 0; i < len(a)-1; i++ {
		s += a[i] * a[i+1]
	}
	return s
}
-- ops_simd.go.want --
//go:build goexperiment.simd

package test

import (
	"simd"
	"unsafe"
)

// Reads one element ahead of the store: nothing the loop writes is read.
func Diff(dst, a []float64) {
	if _loopvecOverlap(dst, a, 0, len(dst)-1, 0, len(dst)-1+1) {
		for i := 0; i < len(dst)-1; i++ {
			dst[i] = a[i+1] - a[i]
		}
	} else {
		if len(dst)-1 > 0 {
			_ = dst[(len(dst)-1)-1]
			_ = a[len(dst)-1]
			_ = a[(len(dst)-1)-1]
			for _i := 0; _i < len(dst)-1; {
				_v1, _n := simd.LoadFloat64sPart(a[_i+1:])
				_v2, _ := simd.LoadFloat64sPart(a[_i : len(dst)-1])
				_v1.Sub(_v2).StorePart(dst[_i : len(dst)-1])
				_i += _n
			}
		}
	}
}

// Reads on both sides, and the same slice at three offsets.
func Smooth(dst, a []int32) {
	if _loopvecOverlap(dst, a, 1, len(dst)-1, 0, len(dst)-1+1) {
		for i := 1; i < len(dst)-1; i++ {
			dst[i] = a[i-1] + a[i] + a[i+1]
		}
	} else {
		if len(dst)-1 > 1 {
			_ = dst[(len(dst)-1)-1]
			_ = a[(len(dst)-1)-2]
			_ = a[(len(dst)-1)-1]
			_ = a[len(dst)-1]
			for _i := 1; _i < len(dst)-1; {
				_v1, _n := simd.LoadInt32sPart(a[_i-1:])
				_v2, _ := simd.LoadInt32sPart(a[_i : len(dst)-1])
				_v3, _ := simd.LoadInt32sPart(a[_i+1:])
				_v1.Add(_v2).Add(_v3).StorePart(dst[_i : len(dst)-1])
				_i += _n
			}
		}
	}
}

// The offset is a variable.
func Shift(dst, a []int32, off int) {
	_vcInt32s2 := simd.BroadcastInt32s(2)
	if _loopvecOverlap(dst, a) {
		for i := 0; i < len(dst); i++ {
			dst[i] = a[i+off] * 2
		}
	} else {
		if len(dst) > 0 {
			_ = a[len(dst)+off-1]
			for _i := 0; _i < len(dst); {
				_v1, _n := simd.LoadInt32sPart(a[_i+off:])
				_v1.Mul(_vcInt32s2).StorePart(dst[_i:])
				_i += _n
			}
		}
	}
}

// A copy from an offset.
func CopyShift(dst, src []int32) {
	if _loopvecOverlap(dst, src) {
		for i := 0; i < len(dst); i++ {
			dst[i] = src[i+1]
		}
	} else {
		if len(dst) > 0 {
			_ = src[len(dst)]
			copy(dst, src[1:])
		}
	}
}

func CopyBehind(dst, src []int32) {
	if _loopvecOverlap(dst, src, 2, len(dst), 0, len(dst)) {
		for i := 2; i < len(dst); i++ {
			dst[i] = src[i-2]
		}
	} else {
		if len(dst) > 2 {
			_ = src[len(dst)-3]
			copy(dst[2:], src[0:])
		}
	}
}

// A reduction over neighboring elements.
func SumPairs(a []int32) int32 {
	var s int32
	if len(a)-1 > 0 {
		_ = a[(len(a)-1)-1]
		_ = a[len(a)-1]
		{
			_i := 0
			if len(a)-1 >= 64 {
				_a1 := simd.BroadcastInt32s(0)
				_lanes := _a1.Len()
				for ; _i+_lanes <= len(a)-1; _i += _lanes {
					_v1 := simd.LoadInt32s(a[_i:])
					_v2 := simd.LoadInt32s(a[_i+1:])
					_a1 = _a1.Add(_v1.Mul(_v2))
				}
				var _buf1 [16]int32
				_a1.Store(_buf1[:])
				for _, _x := range _buf1[:_lanes] {
					s = s + _x
				}
			}
			for i := _i; i < len(a)-1; i++ {
				s += a[i] * a[i+1]
			}
		}
	}
	return s
}

func _loopvecOverlap[T any](a, b []T, window ...int) bool {
	aLo, aHi, bLo, bHi := 0, len(a), 0, len(b)
	if len(window) == 4 {
		aLo, aHi, bLo, bHi = window[0], window[1], window[2], window[3]
	}
	if aLo >= aHi || bLo >= bHi {
		return false
	}
	size := unsafe.Sizeof(a[0])
	aBase := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(a)))
	bBase := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(unsafe.SliceData(b)))
	aStart, aEnd := aBase+uintptr(aLo)*size, aBase+uintptr(aHi)*size
	bStart, bEnd := bBase+uintptr(bLo)*size, bBase+uintptr(bHi)*size
	return aStart < bEnd && bStart < aEnd
}
-- testmain/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/test"
)

var sizes = []int{0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 16, 17, 33, 64, 65, 100, 131}

func ramp32(n int, scale int32) []int32 {
	s := make([]int32, n)
	for i := range s {
		s[i] = int32(i*i+1) * scale
	}
	return s
}

func fill(n int, v int32) []int32 {
	s := make([]int32, n)
	for i := range s {
		s[i] = v
	}
	return s
}

func sum32(s []int32) (t int64) {
	for i, v := range s {
		t += int64(v) * int64(i+1)
	}
	return t
}

func try(f func()) (panicked bool) {
	defer func() { panicked = recover() != nil }()
	f()
	return false
}

// out is what a loop left in dst, or 0 when it panicked: the rewritten loops check
// the lengths first and write nothing, where the scalar loop has written what
// came before the bad index. Only the panic is the same.
func out(panicked bool, dst []int32) int64 {
	if panicked {
		return 0
	}
	return sum32(dst)
}

func main() {
	for _, n := range sizes {
		a := ramp32(n+4, 3)

		d1, d2 := fill(n, -1), fill(n, -1)
		p1 := try(func() { test.Smooth(d1, a) })
		p2 := try(func() { test.CopyShift(d2, a) })
		fmt.Println(n, "A", p1, out(p1, d1), p2, out(p2, d2))

		// A source too short by one must panic.
		short := ramp32(n, 3)
		d3, d4 := fill(n, -1), fill(n, -1)
		p3 := try(func() { test.CopyShift(d3, short) })
		p4 := try(func() { test.Smooth(d4, short[:max(n-1, 0)]) })
		fmt.Println(n, "S", p3, out(p3, d3), p4, out(p4, d4))

		d5 := fill(n, -1)
		p5 := try(func() { test.CopyBehind(d5, a) })
		fmt.Println(n, "B", p5, out(p5, d5), test.SumPairs(a), test.SumPairs(a[:n]))

		for _, off := range []int{0, 1, 3, 4, 5, -1} {
			d := fill(n, -1)
			p := try(func() { test.Shift(d, a, off) })
			fmt.Println(n, "O", off, p, out(p, d))
		}

		f := make([]float64, n)
		for i := range f {
			f[i] = float64(i*i) * 0.5
		}
		df := make([]float64, n)
		pf := try(func() { test.Diff(df, f) })
		var t float64
		for i, v := range df {
			t += v * float64(i+1)
		}
		if pf {
			t = 0
		}
		fmt.Println(n, "D", pf, t)

		// The views overlap, so the original loop runs.
		buf := ramp32(n+3, 1)
		po := try(func() { test.Shift(buf[:n], buf[1:], 1) })
		fmt.Println(n, "V", po, out(po, buf))
	}
}

-- ops.go.guarded --
//go:build !goexperiment.simd

package test

// Reads one element ahead of the store: nothing the loop writes is read.
func Diff(dst, a []float64) {
	for i := 0; i < len(dst)-1; i++ {
		dst[i] = a[i+1] - a[i]
	}
}

// Reads on both sides, and the same slice at three offsets.
func Smooth(dst, a []int32) {
	for i := 1; i < len(dst)-1; i++ {
		dst[i] = a[i-1] + a[i] + a[i+1]
	}
}

// The offset is a variable.
func Shift(dst, a []int32, off int) {
	for i := 0; i < len(dst); i++ {
		dst[i] = a[i+off] * 2
	}
}

// A copy from an offset.
func CopyShift(dst, src []int32) {
	for i := 0; i < len(dst); i++ {
		dst[i] = src[i+1]
	}
}

func CopyBehind(dst, src []int32) {
	for i := 2; i < len(dst); i++ {
		dst[i] = src[i-2]
	}
}

// A reduction over neighboring elements.
func SumPairs(a []int32) int32 {
	var s int32
	for i := 0; i < len(a)-1; i++ {
		s += a[i] * a[i+1]
	}
	return s
}
